name: Scream
label: Dischord
lede: Two brothers from the Virginia suburbs who put out Dischord's first full-length album by a single band, were one of the first American hardcore bands to tour Europe, and gave a 17-year-old named Dave Grohl his first real gig.

eras.title: Rock and roll in a hardcore town
eras.text: Scream came together in Bailey's Crossroads, Virginia, and found the D.C. punk and new wave scene the way a lot of suburban kids did: through Bad Brains. What set them apart early was a rock and roll streak the city bands didn't have and didn't want.

years.h: The Stahl brothers start a band in Bailey's Crossroads
years.p: [[Pete Stahl|9241a075-b363-477a-88ba-dfa8910b0b13]] sings, his brother [[Franz Stahl|b41d6d0a-bfd7-4927-96cf-7273a320d02a]] plays guitar, [[Skeeter Thompson|f308929f-4345-4c02-b2fe-0871c7762c8b]] plays bass. [[Kent Stax|c1e2187d-d4c7-428f-a4c8-3b4043f31591]] takes over the drums from original drummer Steve Atton not long after the start.

eras.title: The first full-length
eras.text: Dischord had put out singles, a sampler and a split LP when Scream handed it a whole album of their own. They followed it with a heavier record, a second guitarist, and trips overseas that almost no American hardcore band was making yet.

years.h: Still Screaming · Dischord No. 9
years.p: Scream cut the 17 songs at Inner Ear in 1982 with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] and Don Zientara. Released in 1983, it's the first full-length on Dischord by a single band.
years.xp:
Up to this point Dischord had released singles, the Flex Your Head sampler and the Faith/Void split. Still Screaming was a different kind of statement: one band, one long-player, with a streak of rock and roll that the straight hardcore bands around them left alone.

Dischord re-cut the LP in March 2009, and it has stayed in print.

years.h: Live at Ebony Hall, Winnipeg, September 11, 1983
yt: Live at Ebony Hall, Winnipeg, September 11, 1983

years.h: This Side Up, and a second guitar
years.p: For their second album, This Side Up, Scream add [[Robert Lee "Harley" Davidson|01bf2142-0999-4077-8a59-11256ff80016]] as a second guitarist in the studio and on stage.

years.h: Scream tour Europe and the UK, ahead of most US hardcore
years.p: Scream tour hard across the US, then Europe and the UK. Dischord calls them one of the first American hardcore bands to make that trip.

eras.title: The kid on the drums
eras.text: When Kent Stax left in 1986, Scream hired Dave Grohl, a teenager from the local scene who fibbed about his age to get the job. Four years later the band came apart on the road and Grohl went north to Seattle to join Nirvana.

years.h: A 17-year-old named [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]] gets the gig
years.p: Kent Stax leaves Scream for personal reasons. Dave Grohl auditions, tells the band he's older than he is so they'll take him on tour, and drops out of high school in his junior year to go.

years.h: Banging the Drum · Dischord No. 25
years.p: Scream's third album, and the last with Kent Stax on drums.

years.h: Dave Grohl drums for Iggy Pop in Toronto
years.p: On a 1987 Scream tour stop in Toronto, [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]] ends up drumming for [[Iggy Pop|f37b3f31-b1f8-4b88-8cb5-b34f709b17d7]] at a CD release event.

years.h: No More Censorship, on a reggae label
years.p: Dave Grohl's first studio album with Scream. The band puts it out on RAS Records, a reggae label, instead of Dischord.

years.h: Scream's show in Alzey, Germany, becomes a live album
years.p: On Scream's spring 1990 European tour, a show in Alzey, Germany, is recorded and becomes Your Choice Live Series Vol. 10.

years.h: Skeeter Thompson quits mid-tour and Scream end in L.A.
years.p: Bassist [[Skeeter Thompson|f308929f-4345-4c02-b2fe-0871c7762c8b]] quits Scream mid-tour in 1990 and the band falls apart. Dave Grohl, broke and stranded in Los Angeles, calls Buzz Osborne of [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]].
years.xp:
Pete and Franz Stahl stayed in North Hollywood and started Wool.

On an earlier West Coast run, Grohl had become friends with [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]], and Buzz Osborne had brought [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] and [[Krist Novoselic|ac05e29f-0561-4445-bb26-5562d2389531]] to see Scream play. With the band suddenly gone, Grohl phoned Osborne, who told him [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] needed a drummer and passed along their number.

Grohl moved to Seattle and joined Nirvana that year.

eras.title: One more record, one more Christmas
eras.text: Scream's last studio album of the original run, Fumble, came out three years after the band stopped, with Dave Grohl, by then in Nirvana, on drums. After that came one-off reunions, including a December 1996 show at the Black Cat in D.C.

years.h: Fumble · Dischord No. 83
years.p: Scream record Fumble at Inner Ear with Eli Janney producing, and it comes out three years after the breakup. Dave Grohl wrote and sang Gods Look Down.

years.h: Scream's Fumble line-up tours North America
years.p: Pete Stahl, Franz Stahl, Skeeter Thompson and Dave Grohl go back out as Scream to support Fumble.

years.h: Scream reunite at the Dragonfly with Zack de la Rocha
years.p: Scream play a one-off reunion show at the Dragonfly in Los Angeles, and [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]] singer Zack de la Rocha joins them on stage.

years.h: Scream's Christmas reunion at the Black Cat
years.p: Scream come home for a holiday show at the Black Cat in Washington, D.C. The night is released in 1998 as Live at the Black Cat on Torque Records.

eras.title: The original four, and a last goodbye
eras.text: The original line-up came back together and stayed together, with Dave Grohl now hosting them rather than drumming. Their final album, DC Special, became a portrait of D.C. music across six decades, and it arrived weeks after the death of original drummer Kent Stax.

years.h: Scream's original line-up reunites at the Black Cat
years.p: Pete Stahl, Franz Stahl, Skeeter Thompson and Kent Stax share one stage again as Scream, at the Black Cat in Washington, D.C.

years.h: Scream play the 9:30 Club's 30th birthday
years.p: An ad hoc Scream line-up plays the 9:30 Club's 30th anniversary celebration in Washington, D.C.

years.h: Complete Control Sessions, live at Studio 606
years.p: Seven songs recorded live by John Lousteau with Scream's original line-up at [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]]'s Studio 606 in Los Angeles. Grohl, once their drummer, is now the host.

years.h: The reunited Scream tour Europe again
years.p: Scream go back to Europe, more than twenty years after their last European tour in 1990.

years.h: No More Censorship back in print
years.p: Scream's 1988 album, Dave Grohl's first studio record with the band, gets a reissue.

q: Kent is the original heartbeat of Scream.
years.h: Scream drummer Kent Stax dies at 61
years.p: Kent Stax, drummer on Scream's first three albums, dies after a bout with metastatic cancer, the band said. They called him irreplaceable, and a fisherman, carpenter and train enthusiast.
years.xp:
Stax joined not long after the band formed and played on Still Screaming, This Side Up and Banging the Drum. The band's statement used his given name, Bennett Kent Stacks. He came back for the reunions, played in other bands including The Suspects and the Daryl Davis Band, and was married to his wife Andrea for 40 years.

His death came days after Scream announced DC Special. [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]] dedicated Everlong to him at a Foo Fighters show, Consequence reported.

years.h: [[Jerry Busher|59c39d46-efd2-4fa0-912e-93ead7a4ab97]] replaces Kent Stax in Scream
years.p: Jerry Busher, a longtime D.C. drummer who also plays on Scream's DC Special, takes over from Kent Stax.

years.h: DC Special · Dischord No. 194
years.p: Scream's last album, recorded by Don Zientara at Inner Ear shortly before the studio was evicted, with guests from six decades of D.C. music, among them [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]], [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]], [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]] and Amy Pickering.
years.xp: Scream built the record as a history lesson: the band invited its whole music community in to weave the story of Washington music into the story of Scream. It was also one of the last records Zientara made at Inner Ear, forty years after he helped produce Still Screaming.

years.h: "DC Special Sha La La" (official video)
Andrew Black replaces Jerry Busher on drums
years.p: Andrew Black takes over as Scream's drummer after Jerry Busher's stint, per Wikipedia.
